title: Governor of Michigan

context.text: This is an open seat: Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer is term-limited and cannot seek a third term.

In the August 4 primaries, Jocelyn Benson won the Democratic nomination with 83.2% over Genesee County Sheriff Chris Swanson, and John James won the Republican nomination with 50.1% over businessman Perry Johnson.
Former Detroit Mayor Mike Duggan ended his independent campaign for governor on May 21, 2026.

candidates.name: Jocelyn Benson
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Winnie Brinks, Michigan Senate Majority Leader. Won the August 4 Democratic primary with 83.2%.

summary.text: Jocelyn Benson is Michigan's Secretary of State and the Democratic nominee for governor, with running mate Winnie Brinks. A former Wayne State University law dean, she was elected secretary of state in 2018 and re-elected in 2022. Her campaign emphasizes housing, health-care costs, child care and education, and she has said she would pass gun-safety legislation.

background.text: Raised in Pittsburgh; B.A. from Wellesley College, a master's as a Marshall Scholar at Oxford, and a J.D. from Harvard Law School.
Taught at Wayne State University Law School from 2005 and served as its dean from 2012 to 2016; later led the Ross Initiative in Sports for Equality (2016-2018).
Lost the 2010 race for secretary of state, then won the office in 2018 and was re-elected in 2022.

priorities.text: Housing: building more homes faster and cutting red tape in housing processes; her housing page names corporate investors and out-of-state speculators as part of the problem.
priorities.quote: That means building more homes, faster.

priorities.text: Health-care costs: low- or no-cost preventive care, an independent Prescription Drug Affordability Board, cost-transparency legislation, and medical debt relief.
Child care: her page describes low pay for child care workers and a shortage of providers as problems, and calls for affordable, reliable early learning and care.

positions.summary: At a May 2026 gun-violence prevention forum, Benson said she wants to ensure Michigan is "passing legislation on gun safety"; her campaign says that as governor she will support commonsense laws that keep Michigan communities safe. She has been endorsed by Giffords PAC, Everytown for Gun Safety and Moms Demand Action.
Calls for building more homes faster and names outdated zoning regulations and bureaucratic red tape among the causes of the housing shortage.
positions.quote: That means building more homes, faster.

record.text: Announced that automatic voter registration had launched at Michigan branch offices, implementing the 2018 voter-approved Promote the Vote amendment.

Issued a statewide order prohibiting open carry of firearms at polling places on Election Day 2020; a Court of Claims judge struck down the order in Robert Davis v. Jocelyn Benson, and the attorney general's office said it would appeal.

Released a letter to the Board of State Canvassers describing election-administration policies meant to avoid conflicts of interest arising from her dual role as secretary of state and candidate for governor.

candidates.name: John James
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Jay DeBoyer, state representative from the 63rd district. Won the August 4 Republican primary with 50.1% over Perry Johnson; endorsed by President Trump.

summary.text: John James is the U.S. Representative for Michigan's 10th District and the Republican nominee for governor, with running mate Jay DeBoyer. A West Point graduate and former Army Apache pilot, he led his family's logistics company before running for the U.S. Senate in 2018 and 2020 and winning his House seat in 2022. His platform calls for eliminating the state income tax, lower energy costs, school choice and a parents' bill of rights, and full funding for law enforcement.

background.text: Born in Southfield and raised in Detroit; graduated from West Point in 2004 and served eight years in the Army as an aviation officer, including Iraq combat tours.
Master's degree from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan; became president of James Group International, a Detroit supply-chain company.
Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in 2018 and 2020 (lost to Debbie Stabenow and Gary Peters); elected to the U.S. House in 2022 and re-elected in 2024.

priorities.text: Eliminating the state income tax by cutting what he calls waste and fraud in Lansing.
priorities.quote: We are eliminating the state income tax.

priorities.text: Lowering energy costs: holding residential bill growth at or below inflation, replacing Michigan Public Service Commission commissioners, and repealing PA 235.
Education: a Parents' Bill of Rights and an expanded school choice agenda.

positions.summary: At a May 2026 Republican candidate forum, Bridge Michigan reported that all of the candidates, including James, said they were pro-life and opposed the 2022 ballot measure that enshrined abortion protections in Michigan's constitution.

His education agenda says he will opt Michigan into the federal K-12 Education Freedom Tax Credit and expand charter school options; his Parents' Bill of Rights says parents can choose alternative education options such as homeschooling or charter schools.
positions.quote: Parents can choose alternative education options, such as homeschooling or charter schools, without excessive regulation or targeting.

positions.summary: Pledges to fully fund law enforcement and has been endorsed by the Police Officers Association of Michigan and the Fraternal Order of Police of Michigan.
positions.quote: As Governor, John James will FULLY FUND law enforcement, Back The Blue

record.text: Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, including its subcommittees on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Energy; and Health.
Introduced the Patients Deserve Price Tags Act with bipartisan co-sponsors to strengthen hospital and health-coverage price transparency requirements.

Introduced the Tariff Relief for American Development and Employment Act (TRADE Act), which would set aside a portion of tariff revenue for reshoring funds and temporary relief to businesses that can show economic harm.

candidates.name: Anthony Hudson
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Beau Parmenter. Nominated at the Libertarian convention.

summary.text: Anthony Hudson is a Genesee County truck driver and the Libertarian nominee for governor, with running mate Beau Parmenter; he initially sought the Republican nomination for governor before switching to the Libertarian Party in February. On September 29, 2026 the Libertarian Party of Michigan released a statement disavowing him, saying his campaign's ideology contradicts the party's core values, platform and purpose; Hudson said he was comfortable with the disavowal. His name remains on the ballot on the Libertarian line because the withdrawal deadline had passed.

priorities.text: No data centers or Flock cameras.
priorities.quote: No Data Centers or Flock cameras

positions.summary: In his Vote411 answer on immigration he says people in the country illegally will be removed.
positions.quote: If you are here illegally, we will remove you.

candidates.researchNotes: Sources are his Vote411 questionnaire answers plus news reports of the Libertarian Party's disavowal. No campaign website found (the Vote411 page lists his running mate's site, BeauParmenter.com, which was not read). No statements found on abortion, guns or other guide issues.

statements.quote: We would open and use our nuclear power plants, fix and use our Hydro dams, we would approve line 5 and we would burn the trash coming in from Canada!
statements.context: In his answer to the League of Women Voters Vote411 questionnaire, on energy
In his answer to the League of Women Voters Vote411 questionnaire, listed among his top three priorities

candidates.name: Douglas Campbell
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Bobbie Clay. Nominated at the Green Party convention.

summary.text: Douglas Campbell is the Green Party nominee for governor, with running mate Bobbie Clay.

positions.summary: In his Vote411 answer on education he says to eliminate the charter system.
In his Vote411 answer on the economy he calls for a not-for-profit national health system, starting at the state level.
positions.quote: We need to create a not-for-profit National Health System.

candidates.researchNotes: Sources are his Vote411 questionnaire answers (he has no campaign website; the page lists the state party's site). A speech on indexing the minimum wage was reported in a search summary only and was not read, so it is not used.

statements.quote: Every flat roof and parking lot should be covered with photovoltaic collectors, and the energy they put onto the grid paid for on a net-metering basis.
statements.context: In his answer to the League of Women Voters Vote411 questionnaire, on energy

statements.quote: Immigrants built the United States. Almost everybody here is either an immigrant or descendants of immigrants. We need to dial down the hysteria and realize that wage suppression is the result of late-stage capitalism, not immigration.
statements.context: In his answer to the League of Women Voters Vote411 questionnaire, on immigration

candidates.name: Donna Brandenburg
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Robert Donald Cowper II. Nominated at the U.S. Taxpayers convention.

summary.text: Donna Brandenburg is the U.S. Taxpayers Party nominee for governor, with running mate Robert Donald Cowper II.

priorities.text: Honesty in government through complete financial and governmental department audits.
priorities.quote: honesty in government through complete financial and governmental department audits

priorities.text: Ending the property tax and income tax, which she calls unlawful.
priorities.quote: End unlawful property tax and income tax.

priorities.text: Defending against corruption and multinational special interests, with a focus on local business, job creation and conservation.
priorities.quote: Defend against corruption and multinational special interest/corporations with a focus returned to local business, job creation, conservation

candidates.researchNotes: Sources are her Vote411 questionnaire answers. Her listed site, BrandenburgForGovernor.com, did not load readable issue pages. No statement taking a side on a guide issue statement was found.

statements.quote: Lawful immigration is a core tenet of the American process. The Constitution guards against government usurpation of rights.
statements.context: In her answer to the League of Women Voters Vote411 questionnaire, on immigration

statements.quote: I will stop policies that pad utility bills and end backroom deals which destroy the ecology of Michigan.
statements.context: In her answer to the League of Women Voters Vote411 questionnaire, on environment and energy

statements.quote: End unlawful property tax and income tax.
statements.context: In her answer to the League of Women Voters Vote411 questionnaire, on her priorities

researchNotes: Running mates (Winnie Brinks, Jay DeBoyer, Beau Parmenter, Bobbie Clay, Robert Donald Cowper II) are elected jointly with the governor candidate and are noted in each candidate's ballotNote rather than listed separately. The Michigan Department of State's candidate listing could not be loaded from this environment. The five-candidate governor slate (Benson D, James R, Hudson L, Brandenburg U.S. Taxpayers, Campbell Green) was confirmed against the Saginaw County Clerk's candidate list for the Nov. 3 general election (a county clerk list marked unofficial), and also matches Bridge Michigan's ballot guide and Wikipedia's election page. Federal roll-call votes for Rep. James are not included (added later by script).
